summary: Decoded the mechanism by which wpcmk renders skill names in the character-creation UI. Skill names are stored as Huffman-compressed messages in msg.dbs. The 82-entry skill table at wroot.exe file offset 0x1005e drives both the skill-availability picker and the name lookup. msg_id = skill_table_index + 0xfa0 (4000). Skill names live in msg.dbs slots 7-8, msg IDs 4000..4080 (entry 4025 is a confirmed gap). Null holes at SKILL_SLOT_NAMES positions 10 and 17-21 are confirmed via all 6 stock characters having zero values at those positions in pcfile.dbs.

findings.claim: Skill name msg_id = 82-table index + 0xfa0 (= 4000). The engine computes this at wpcmk 0x2248 before calling draw_msg_in_window.

disassembly: 05 a0 0f  ; add ax, 0x0fa0   ; ax = skill_table_index + 4000 = msg_id
evidence.context: This instruction is inside the skill-selection UI render path at wpcmk 0x21db. ax holds the skill table index (0..81) from the filtered available-skills buffer built by function 0x2186. After this add, the code calls draw_msg_in_window via thunk 0xc2db.

findings.claim: The 82-entry skill master table lives at wroot.exe file offset 0x1005e (DGROUP 0x00de at runtime). Each entry is 6 bytes: [group, level, category, max, max2, pillar_flags]. 79 real entries; entries 79-81 are zero-padded.

evidence.notes: Entry 0 bytes: group/level fields consistent with Sword (weaponry). Pillar flags encode MAGIC(bit3)/FAITH(bit2)/PHYSICAL(bit1)/MENTAL(bit0). Verified non-zero entries 0..78; entries 79-81 all zero.

findings.claim: Skill name messages occupy msg IDs 4000..4024 (slot 7, dbs_offset 0x32b) and 4026..4080 (slot 8, dbs_offset 0x0). Entry at msg_id 4025 is a confirmed gap — no msg.hdr entry covers it.

evidence.msg_hdr_format: 2-byte count (718) + 718 x 6-byte entries: (start_id u16 LE, dbs_offset u16 LE, count u8, file_slot u8)
evidence.gap_at_4025: No entry in msg.hdr covers msg_id 4025 — this is a genuine gap in the skill name table. Corresponds to SKILL_SLOT_NAMES[25] = null (slot 25 is between 'Skulduggery' slot 15 and 'Scouting' slot 22 in the 30-slot class availability bitmaps).
evidence.notes: msg.dbs data is Huffman-compressed; actual strings not decoded in this pass (requires a live save state in character creation mode to access the in-memory tree). The gap at 4025 is independently confirmed by msg.hdr having no entry covering that ID.

findings.claim: SKILL_SLOT_NAMES positions 10 and 17-21 are genuine holes (null). All 6 stock characters have zero values at those character record positions.
Non-null SKILL_SLOT_NAMES values cross-validate correctly against stock character skill levels in pcfile.dbs
The thunk at wpcmk address 0xc2db targets wroot.exe function draw_msg_in_window at wroot file offset 0x083f

unresolved: Actual decoded skill name strings from msg.dbs slots 7-8 — the Huffman tree is only loaded in memory during active character creation (wpcmk mode). No save states captured during character creation; the tree was all 0xffff (uninitialized) in all 13 available save states. The SKILL_SLOT_NAMES values in class-skill-availability.ts ('Sword', 'Axe', 'Polearm', etc.) are from martydill's open-source RE repo and cross-validate positionally against stock chars but are not yet binary-decoded from msg.dbs.

Slot 25 appears as null in SKILL_SLOT_NAMES but the msg.hdr gap at 4025 vs the 30-slot class availability array needs reconciliation — the 82-table and the 30-slot availability bitmap use different index spaces. The mapping from 30-slot class-availability index to 82-table skill index is not fully decoded.
Whether msg_id 4025 being missing from msg.hdr means that 82-table entry 25 has no human-readable name, or whether the table index and msg_id are not in strict 1:1 correspondence for all entries.
